title: CAM-54 slice: codex reviewer confabulates the review - force diff-grounding by injecting git diff main...HEAD into the codex reviewer prompt
description:
LIVE FINDING (slice-4 de-risk probe, 2026-07-19): dispatched the real codex reviewer argv (rendered via CodexAdapter.buildSpawnArgv('reviewer'), model gpt-5.5, -c model_instructions_file=<stripped subagent-reviewer.md>, REVIEWER_TASK_PROMPT) against a scratch branch whose ONLY diff vs main was a 4-line doc file. Result: codex faithfully WROTE a schema-valid scripts/cam/review-report.json (verdict CLEAN, findings[], artifactOfRecord) AND review-artifact.txt -- but it reviewed the WRONG changeset. The artifact header read 'Branch: cam/issue-352 (CAM-352 ...)' (already merged, NOT on the scratch branch), the single finding was about codex-auth.test.ts (not in the diff), and the Layer-B oracle lines were fabricated ('bun test: 5131 pass / 0 fail across 290 files'). codex NEVER ran git diff main...HEAD; it pattern-matched to repo/context and confabulated a confident CLEAN verdict about code not under review. This is the most dangerous failure mode: the sidecar would parse <review>CLEAN</review> and ship on a review that never looked at the real diff.

ROOT CAUSE: ADR-0047 mismatch (d) -- codex has no --agent harness that forces the reviewer's grounding steps. The claude reviewer reliably runs `git diff main...HEAD` itself via its Bash tool + agent harness; codex, fed the same body as a plain developer prompt via -c model_instructions_file, does not.

FIX (recommended): the CodexAdapter reviewer path should pre-compute the actual `git diff main...HEAD` (and/or the changed-file list) and inject it into the reviewer prompt/instructions so codex physically has the diff to review, rather than trusting it to self-fetch. A stronger imperative directive ('run git diff main...HEAD FIRST and review ONLY that diff') is a cheaper fallback but relies on the same obedience codex just ignored, so injection is the robust option. Scope this to the codex (reviewer) path only; the claude path must stay byte-identical.

SECONDARY OBSERVATIONS (not this slice's scope, file/track separately if pursued): (1) codex reviewer was very slow (>10min, did not complete) at xhigh reasoning while running full gates; the sidecar review timeout must accommodate codex or tune reasoning effort. (2) <review> sentinel-to-pane streaming is unconfirmed -- piped stdout block-buffers and the run was killed before flush; needs a real TTY/tmux-pane capture test once grounding is fixed. Both are moot until the reviewer actually reviews the right diff.

PREREQUISITE ORDERING: this slice must land before the slice-4 live ceremony (a codex CLEAN is meaningless until it reviews the real diff) and before slice-5 (per-backend model-id decoupling). Also note the config-flip ceremony is separately blocked by drift-guard tests (models.test.ts drift guard pins reviewer to a known claude model; review.test.ts dispatch-shape tests read the real project.toml) -- making project.toml codex-tolerant is slice-5's job.

spec.scope: Fix the codex reviewer's confabulation (proven live: fed the reviewer agent body via -c model_instructions_file, codex did NOT run git diff main...HEAD and reviewed an unrelated already-merged branch, emitting a confident CLEAN). In the CodexAdapter reviewer path only (src/supervisor/backend-adapter.ts, the 'reviewer' case in buildSpawnArgv -> renderActor), pre-compute the actual branch diff (git diff main...HEAD, plus the changed-file name list) at dispatch time and inject it so codex physically has the diff under review, with an explicit directive to review ONLY that diff. Favor appending the diff to the model_instructions_file body (file-based, no argv-size limit) over stuffing it into the shell-escaped prompt argument. The ClaudeAdapter path for all four actors must remain byte-identical; the claude reviewer already self-grounds via its Bash tool. Scope the injection to the codex reviewer actor only, not implementer/planner/auditor.
acceptanceCriteria: The codex reviewer dispatch physically includes the actual git diff main...HEAD output plus the changed-file list, computed at dispatch time, in the content passed to codex (instructions file body preferred over the argv prompt to avoid ARG_MAX blowups on large diffs).
The codex reviewer instructions/prompt carry an explicit directive to review ONLY the injected diff (the changes on the current branch vs main), not repo context or history.
The ClaudeAdapter rendered argv for reviewer, implementer, planner, and auditor is byte-identical to before this slice; a test asserts the claude reviewer argv is unchanged.
A test against a real fixture git repo with a known diff asserts the rendered codex reviewer dispatch contains the injected diff content (hits the real git boundary, not a fake).
When the branch has no diff vs main, the injected content is a well-formed no-changes marker (never a crash or empty-string ambiguity).
bun run typecheck, bun test, and bun run check:all all pass.
gotchas: The codex reviewer argv is assembled in renderActor (src/supervisor/backend-adapter.ts ~438); the 'reviewer' case is ~427; REVIEWER_TASK_PROMPT is at ~127; writeCodexInstructionsFile (~373) writes the stripped agent body to /tmp.

Prefer appending the diff to the model_instructions_file body (or a sibling /tmp file codex is told to read) over the shell-escaped prompt: git diff can be large and the prompt is a single argv token subject to ARG_MAX.
Do NOT modify ClaudeAdapter rendering; the claude reviewer grounds itself via its own Bash git diff.

git diff main...HEAD (three-dot) reviews branch changes since the merge-base with main, matching the reviewer's 'current branch vs main' contract; verify the base ref name resolution ('main') is robust.
If capping large diffs, do it visibly (a truncation marker), never a silent cut that hides changes.
Live evidence in the issue body: codex confabulated a review of cam/issue-352 with fabricated Layer-B oracle PASS lines while the real diff was a 4-line doc.
